title: More pain for Sydney Trains commuters after tense negotiations with the rail union stalled
text:
Railway workers began an industrial action ‘Go Slow’ on Friday morning By Brett Lackey for Daily Mail Australia
Published: 19:23 GMT, February 13, 2025 | Updated: 19:39 GMT, February 13, 2025
Sydney Trains passengers have been told to wait for delays in the network after the salary negotiations between the NSW government and the stagnant rail union last night.
Railway workers will execute trains 23 km/hour slower on Friday morning after both parties did not reach an agreement during the discussions on Thursday night.
The railway, tram and bus union (RBTU) requires a salary increase of 32 percent for four years.
RTBU NSW secretary, Toby Warnes, told trains passengers to wait for delays and should “direct their anger towards the NSW government for uncertainty.”
The New Wales del Sur government has responded by declaring that any employee who participates in the action ‘go slow’ will have his salary docked.
“Railway workers are ready to come to work, but legal tactics and highly unusual legal threats of the NSW government mean that they lose a whole day salary if they have to reduce the speed in any section of the track,” Warnes said .
‘The great impact that this little action has on travelers on Friday depends on the government.
“We asked the Government to terminate its blocking notices to ensure that the services were carried out without problems on Friday, but unfortunately they refused.”
Sydney trains have been told to wait
Transport for NSW also warned passengers to wait for delays in the train network and allow additional travel time.
“While we expect a minimum interruption, the consequences of industrial action can be unpredictable, as well as the operational needs of the network,” said Transport for NSW in a statement.
“Sydney Trains and NSW Trainlink apologize to our passengers if they experience industrial actions in the railway network.”
